questions.lead: China's Zhang Zhanshuo won the last swimming final of the 2026 Asian Games in a time of 3:41.28.
questions.prompt: How many gold medals did he win at those Games in all?

questions.lead: Zhang Zhanshuo's seventh gold came in 3:41.28, passing the Asian Games record of 3:41.53 that Park Tae-hwan set in 2010.
questions.prompt: In which event did he swim it?

questions.lead: Croatia and Ivory Coast have both joined the Artemis Accords, the U.S.-led principles for exploring the Moon and Mars.
questions.prompt: How many countries have now signed them?

explanations: He won seven, the first athlete to manage that at a single Asian Games. The last of them came in the men's 400 metre freestyle, in a time of 3:41.28.
It was the 400 metre freestyle, on the final day of swimming. His 3:41.28 overtook the Asian Games record of 3:41.53 that Park Tae-hwan set in 2010.
Seventy-five countries have signed the Accords, 34 of them in Europe. Croatia was the 74th, and the accession of Ivory Coast took the total to 75.
The Large Hadron Collider stretches 27 km around. Thousands of magnets of different types steer and control its particle beams.
The new magnets reach 11.3 tesla, about 40% stronger than the fields the current ones produce. Niobium-tin coils are what allow them to do it.

sources.excerpt: In swimming, China's Zhang Zhanshuo becomes the first athlete to win seven gold medals at a single Asian Games, securing his seventh title in the men's 400-metre freestyle with a Games-record time of 3:41.28.

On the final day of swimming, Zhang took the 400 m freestyle with a time of 3:41.28, overtaking the Asian Games record of 3:41.53 Park Tae-hwan set in 2010 and completing his sweep of seven gold medals.
He became the first swimmer in history to win seven golds at a single Asian Games.
Croatia joins the U.S.-led Artemis Accords, becoming the 74th country to do so.

As of September 24, 2026, with the accession of Ivory Coast, 75 countries have signed the Accords, including 34 in Europe, 17 in Asia, 8 in South America, 5 in North America, 9 in Africa, and 2 in Oceania.
Drafted by NASA and the US Department of State, the Accords establish a framework for cooperation in the civil exploration and peaceful use of the Moon, Mars, and other astronomical objects.
CERN Director-General Mark Thomson visited the LHC tunnel to mark the start of the dismantling of the accelerator sections that will be replaced by the new HiLumi LHC components.

The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) stretches 27 km around and relies on thousands of magnets of different types - dipoles, quadrupoles, sextupoles, octupoles, decapoles, etc. - to steer and control its particle beams.

Instead of niobium-titanium, the upgraded magnets use niobium-tin superconducting coils. This allows them to generate magnetic fields reaching 11.3 tesla, about 40% stronger than the fields produced by the current magnets.
